Forge Neo Remi

 A zero-node, conflict-safe, studio-grade AI image creation workbench built on Stable Diffusion WebUI Forge Neo — Anima-first, multi-DiT, and Gradio-free (FastAPI + React 19 SPA). 

English 简体中文

 
 
 
 

 

 

Forge Neo Remi is a downstream distribution of Forge Neo, itself built on Stable Diffusion WebUI Forge and AUTOMATIC1111 WebUI. It is not a node-graph editor and not a new base model: Remi pairs Forge Neo's runtime and modern DiT model stack with a studio-grade, Gradio-free web workbench (FastAPI + SQLite queue + React 19 SPA), declarative capability-driven controls ( remi.ui v1), non-node composable workflows, and deep Anima integration aimed at 8–24 GB consumer GPUs and Apple Silicon unified memory.

 [!IMPORTANT]
 This is an independent downstream branch, not an official release of Forge Neo or any bundled model family. Remi favors integrated, conflict-safe workflows over compatibility with every legacy extension: third-party extensions built for the old Gradio UI must be ported to remi.ui (see Migrating from the Gradio UI).

 Why Remi?

- Studio workbench & capability-driven Generate view. A fast, Gradio-free React 19 SPA with refined light and dark themes, phone layouts, full keyboard control, and reload-free English / 简体中文 switching. ModelCapability automatically folds panels that do not apply to the loaded model family (with clear reasons), shows Model Bar quantization/capability badges ( Diffusers , GGUF , INT8-ConvRot , FP8 , NVFP4 , Turbo , RGBA , Control ), and surfaces actionable pre-submit Workflow Advice chips with one-click fixes.
- Non-node composable workflows (Recipes & Linear Pipelines). Save, share, and apply cross-model Recipes (conflict-checked parameter subsets) and run Linear Multi-Stage Pipelines ( Prompt Upsample → Generate → Refine → Finish ) with content-addressed upstream stage caching—change a downstream refine or upscale parameter and automatically reuse earlier outputs without wiring a node graph.
- End-to-end creative loop. Organize outputs with Gallery Boards , trace parent/child Asset Lineage , inspect two runs via pixel slider plus structured Parameter Diff , check alpha transparency with Lightbox 4-backdrop switching ( B ), Send to Reference Image with model-aware slot badges ( , ref image 0 , ref 0 ), iterate locally via Canvas In-Place Staging , expand prompts with the Multimodal/Local Prompt Upsampler (PUP) , and compose structured layouts in JSON Builder (MOSS-Image, FLUX.3 Layout, and Bria Fibo 2.0 VGL 2.0).
- Anima-first inference & conflict-safe runtime. Full 2B / 2.9B / 3.8B support (28/40/52-block layouts + native Qwen3.5 semantic connector), cross-depth LoRA and ControlNet-LLLite remapping, Control-LoRA / VACE, native samplers, guidance, spatial controls, and Anima Remi Presets safe baselines—with mutually exclusive stacks locked before sampling in both the browser and API (details).
- Worker isolation, multi-GPU pools & Apple Silicon support. Run in-process by default or opt into isolated inference via WorkerProtocol : --worker-process (crash/OOM auto-recovery and zero UI/WebSocket GIL contention), --worker-gpus 0,1 (multi-GPU worker pool), and --worker-mlx (optional Apple Silicon MLX / mflux sidecar). These flags are a preview: they list the workers in the Workers monitor, but the queue does not dispatch to them and still runs every job in-process. Includes Apple Silicon MPS dequantized-weight caching, unified-memory awareness, and the reproducible tools/perf/bench inference.py benchmark suite.
- Stable Extension API v1 & upstream governance. Versioned remi.ui ( REMI API VERSION = "1.0" ), optional remi-extension.json manifests, per-extension Diagnostics (load times, hook/action errors and timeouts), the public remi.testing contract verifier, and automated upstream divergence tracking ( tools/upstream forks.py budget , FORKED 
 Light and dark themes, three resizable panes Anima Remi Presets and capability-gated panels 
 
 Image editor: masks, sketch layers, selections, in-place staging Gallery: boards, lineage, search, stars, parameter diff compare 
 
 Queue: live preview, priorities, linear pipelines & recipes Phone layouts: Generate, Gallery and Queue 

The usage guide describes every page.

 Quick Start

You need Git, Python 3.13 or uv, a PyTorch device (an NVIDIA GPU is the most widely tested; Apple Silicon works through MPS) and Node.js 22.18+ or 24.11+ to build the web interface.

 

Then run ./webui.sh on Linux and macOS, or webui-user.bat on Windows.

The first launch installs Python dependencies, builds webui/dist , and prints Running on local URL: Place checkpoints, VAEs, and text encoders in the matching models/ subfolders, then pick them in the model bar. Optional worker modes ( --worker-process , --worker-gpus 0,1 , --worker-mlx ) can be passed via COMMANDLINE ARGS or python launch.py .

For a first Anima image, open Anima Remi Presets in Generate and apply Official Base/Aesthetic — Safe (Recommended) , or Official Turbo — Fast (CFG 1 · 10 steps) for an Anima-Turbo checkpoint.

The usage guide covers detailed installation ( uv , machines without Node.js, Docker), launch options, where data is stored, keyboard shortcuts, security and remote access, and troubleshooting.

 Supported Model Families

Remi retains Forge Neo's modern-model runtime while adding capability-driven tooling across Tier-1 and Tier-2 DiT families (model & acceleration details):

- Anima & Anima Edit: 2B (28 blocks), 2.9B (40), and 3.8B (52, with native qwen35 4b semantic connector), cross-depth LoRA / ControlNet-LLLite remapping, Control-LoRA / VACE, and Anima RGBA (details; Anima RGBA requires its LoRA and VAE)
- Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-Edit & Qwen-Image-2.1: Base and 8-step Turbo; Diffusers folders, Unsloth FP8 / INT8-ConvRot, and GGUF; lossless cross-step prefix KV cache, bidirectional fused/unfused MLP LoRA mapping, Qwen-2.1 per-block compile, Spectrum forecasting, native 4-channel RGBA generation/mask editing, and Qwen-Image-2.1-F

install.title: Quick Start
install.html:
You need Git, Python 3.13 or uv, a PyTorch device (an NVIDIA GPU is the most widely tested; Apple Silicon works through MPS) and Node.js 22.18+ or 24.11+ to build the web interface.

git clone --branch remi https://github.com/beautifulrem/forge-neo-remi.git forge-neo-remi
cd forge-neo-remi

Then run ./webui.sh on Linux and macOS, or webui-user.bat on Windows.

The first launch installs Python dependencies, builds webui/dist, and prints Running on local URL: http://127.0.0.1:7860/. Place checkpoints, VAEs, and text encoders in the matching models/ subfolders, then pick them in the model bar. Optional worker modes (--worker-process, --worker-gpus 0,1, --worker-mlx) can be passed via COMMANDLINE_ARGS or python launch.py.

For a first Anima image, open Anima Remi Presets in Generate and apply Official Base/Aesthetic — Safe (Recommended), or Official Turbo — Fast (CFG 1 · 10 steps) for an Anima-Turbo checkpoint.

The usage guide covers detailed installation (uv, machines without Node.js, Docker), launch options, where data is stored, keyboard shortcuts, security and remote access, and troubleshooting.
